Title 3—The President
Executive Order 12105 • December 19, 1978
Garnishment of Moneys Payable to Employees of Executive Agencies and the District
of Columbia
By virtue of the authority vested in me by Section 461(a)(1) of the Social  
Security Act, as added by Section 501(c) of the Tax Reduction and Simplifica­
tion Act of 1977 (Public Law 95-30, 91 Stat. 158, 42 U.S.C. 661(a)(1)), and

armed forces, and the Mayor of the District of Columbia with respect to  
employees of the Government thereof, is authorized to promulgate regulations  
for the uniform implementation of Section 459 of the Social Security Act, as  
amended (42 U.S.C. 659), hereinafter referred to as the Act.

Commission pursuant to this Order shall:
(a) Be applicable to the Executive branch of the Government as defined in  
Section 461(a)(1) of the Act (42 U.S.C. 661(a)(1)).

ernment to take the actions prescribed by Sections 461(b)(1), 461(b)(3)(A) and  
461(c) of the Act (42 U.S.C. 661(b)(1), 661(b)(3)(A) and 661(c)).
(c) Require the appropriate officials of the Executive branch of the Gov­
ernment to issue such rules, regulations and directives as are necessary to  
implement the regulations of the United States Civil Service Commission.

1-201. Executive Order No. 11881 of October 3, 1975 is revoked.
1-202. All regulations, directives, or actions taken by the United States  
Civil Service Commission pursuant to Executive Order No. 11881 of October  
3, 1975 shall remain in effect until modified, superseded or revoked by the  
United States Civil Service Commission pursuant to this Order.

research_rationale:
EO 12105 (43 FR 59465; signed 1978-12-19, printed in the Federal Register of 1978-12-21) delegates to the Civil Service Commission, in consultation with the Attorney General, the Secretary of Defense and the Mayor of the District of Columbia, authority to promulgate regulations implementing section 459 of the Social Security Act (42 U.S.C. 659) for legal process against federal and D.C. employees' pay to enforce child-support and alimony obligations; it prescribes three required features of those regulations; it revokes EO 11881; and it preserves regulations issued under EO 11881 until the Commission modifies, supersedes or revokes them. Identity: the held Federal Register text of 43 FR 59465 (PDF page 13) prints 'Executive Order 12105', 'December 19, 1978' and the title 'Garnishment of Moneys Payable to Employees of Executive Agencies and the District of Columbia' (FR Doc. 78-35716). The seven machine clauses are the complete operative inventory: the delegation (printed with the label 1-161, an OCR misreading of 1-101), the lead of section 1-102 and its subsections (a), (b) and (c), the revocation in section 1-201 and the savings sentence in section 1-202. The order has no effective-date, sunset or termination provision. Later events: EO 12107 (44 FR 1055, signed 1978-12-28) lists EO 12105 among the orders in which, by its section 2-101, the words Civil Service Commission are replaced by Office of Personnel Management, and its section 2-404 makes the order effective on 1979-01-01; that is an amendment of the clauses naming the Commission, not an end. The U.S. Code note, the eCFR authority line of 5 CFR part 581 and the Federal Register catalog search disclose no revocation, supersession or other amendment. The delegation and the three content requirements are operative: the Commission's functions passed to the Office of Personnel Management and the regulations they authorize are still in the Code of Federal Regulations under this authority. The revocation of EO 11881 was performed when this order issued. The savings sentence is treated as operative because no held source shows that every regulation preserved by it was later modified, superseded or revoked; that is stated as a limit of the evidence, not a finding of an end.

EO 12208 (45 FR 25789, signed 1980-04-15; FR Doc. 80-11908) delegates to the Secretary of State and the Attorney General the functions of consulting with the Judiciary Committees under sections 101(a)(42)(B) and 207(a), (b), (d) and (e) of the Immigration and Nationality Act, delegates to the U.S. Coordinator for Refugee Affairs the reporting and discussion functions of section 207(d)(1) and directs how the Coordinator acts and notifies the Committees, reserves to the President the determinations and refugee-number decisions under sections 101(a)(42)(B) and 207, and deems earlier actions taken under delegated functions to have been taken under the order. EO 13286 (68 FR 10619, effective 2003-03-01 by its section 92), section 49, strikes the words that introduce 1-101(a) and replaces the Attorney General with the Secretary of Homeland Security in 1-101(a); strikes sections 1-101(b) and 1-102; and redesignates sections 1-103 and 1-104 as 1-102 and 1-103. Result at 2026-10-14: sections 1-101(b), 1-102(a) and 1-102(b) (the Coordinator's functions) ended on 2003-03-01 by EO 13286; the delegation in 1-101 and (a), the reserved functions in 1-103 and the deemed-actions sentence in 1-104 continue, amended and renumbered, as the current U.S. Code note shows. No held source revokes the order.
